summary: James Leibold is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Southern California under Charlotte Furth and has held academic posts at the University of Melbourne and La Trobe University.

James Luther Adams (1901–1994) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he later held a post from circa 1957 to 1968.

James Mallinson is an Indologist. After earning degrees from SOAS and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, he served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS (2013) and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 2023.

James Mark Shields works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He was attested in 2016 as Associate Professor of Comparative Humanities and Asian Thought at Bucknell University and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein, attested in 2006.

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard, he completed his PhD under Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil, and held posts at USC and Cornell.

James Miller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who completed an MA at Cambridge (1997) and a PhD at Boston University (2000). In 2014, he was attested as Professor at Queen's University at Kingston.
James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler. He held a post as Librarian at the University of Oxford, attested between 1917 and 1920.

James Murdoch (1856–1921) worked in Japanology and history. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and under Theodor Benfey, later holding posts at Kanazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Kagoshima University.

James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the Banaras Mint and the Kolkata Mint, led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), and founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

James Robert Ballantyne (1813–1864) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Edinburgh. He served at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, as Principal of Benares Sanskrit College, and as India Office librarian.

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford. He taught at Williams College and Michigan before joining Harvard, where he became Harvard-Yenching Institute Director in 2024.

James Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at California State University (attested 1998) and served as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

James Smith Reid (1846–1926) was an ancient historian. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held fellowships and posts across Cambridge colleges, including Christ's College, Pembroke College, and Gonville and Caius College (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was a scholar in history and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Oxford, he held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1871 to 1874.

James Tod (1782–1835) was a scholar of Indology and history who served in the East India Company and studied under Gyanchandra. He later served as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

James W. Benson is an Indologist who taught James McHugh and Susan J. Rosenfield. He was an Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. After earning his PhD from Cambridge, he held long-term posts at Nanzan University and the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (circa 1978–2020).
James Ward (1843–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He taught Surendranath Dasgupta and held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 until 1925.
James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and held a post as Professor of Religion at Stephens College, attested in 2000.
